'''Geoffrey Fryer''' {{post-nominals|FRS}}<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Boxshall |first1=G. A. |title=Geoffrey Fryer. 06 August 1927—18 March 2024: 6 August 1927 — 18 March 2024 |journal=Biographical Memoirs of Fellows of the Royal Society |date=22 April 2025 |doi=10.1098/rsbm.2024.0041|doi-access=free }}</ref> (6 August 1927 – 18 March 2024) was a British biologist.<ref name="www24">{{cite web |title=Fryer, Dr Geoffrey |url=https://www.ukwhoswho.com/display/10.1093/ww/9780199540884.001.0001/ww-9780199540884-e-16548 |website=WHO WAS WHO 2024 |access-date=14 September 2024}}{{dead link|date=May 2025}}</ref>

==Life and career==
Fryer was born in [[Huddersfield, Yorkshire]] on 6 August 1927. He attended [[Huddersfield College]], and then the [[University of London]].<ref name="www24"/>

Fryer was the Deputy Chief Scientific Officer at the Windermere Laboratory, and then at the Freshwater Biological Association from 1981 to 1988. He was also an Honorary Professor at the [[University of Lancaster]] from 1988.

In 1953, Fryer married Vivienne Hodgson. Together they had one son and one daughter. Fryer died on 18 March 2024, at the age of 96.<ref name="www24"/><ref>{{cite web |title=Professor Geoffrey Fryer FRS |url=https://royalsociety.org/people/geoffrey-fryer-11471/ |website=The Royal Society |access-date=14 September 2024}}</ref>

==Honours==
Fryer was elected a [[Fellow of the Royal Society]] in 1972, awarded the Zoological Society of London [[Frink Medal]] in 1983, and the [[Linnean Medal]] in 1987.<ref name="www24"/>

==Tribute==
Fish named after Fryer:
*The cichlid ''[[Alticorpus geoffreyi]]'' <small>[[Jos Snoeks|Snoeks]] & [[Rhoda Walapa|Walapa]] 2004</small>{{fcn|date=May 2025}}
*The Lake Malawi cichlid ''[[Sciaenochromis fryeri]]'' <small>[[Ad Konings|Konings]], 1993</small>{{fcn|date=May 2025}}
